stem: Rohan reads that Mayan landmark numbers are $1$, $20$, $360$, $7200$, and so on, written in vertical place value with a zero symbol.

parts.text: Which claim correctly classifies this place-value system?

options.text: It is a pure base-$20$ system because every place is exactly a power of $20$.
It is almost base-$20$: places use $20$ for the second landmark, but $360$ (not $400$) breaks a pure power-of-$20$ tower, while still using vertical place value and zero.
The zero symbol alone turns any vertical list into base-$10$.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

part_answers.answer: After 1 and 20, the next landmark is 360 rather than 20²=400, so the system is almost base-20, not a pure power-of-20 tower, even though it keeps vertical places and a zero.

teacher.key_rationale: 360≠400 so Mayan place value is almost base-20, not pure base-20. Zero and vertical layout do not force base-10.
